transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Hello. My mind just won’t stop going over everything that could go wrong at work, and I can’t seem to turn the worrying off anymore.
Can you tell me if these worries about work are triggered by a specific event or situation, or have they been ongoing for a while without any clear cause?

These worries have been ongoing for a little over a year now, starting when I was promoted to lead our digital preservation and oral history initiative. While that promotion was the initial trigger, the anxiety has since become a constant, daily presence tied to the ongoing demands and deadlines of the role. It is just there all the time now, rather than being about one specific event.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain tasks or responsibilities at work, or even avoiding work altogether, because of these worries?

Yes, I've started missing internal deadlines and even avoiding some of the community events I'm supposed to lead. I get so keyed up and spend so much time staying home to recheck my work that I end up putting off these important responsibilities. It has really started to get in the way of my job.
Can you describe how these worries and avoidance behaviors have affected your personal relationships and daily activities outside of work?

It’s really taken a toll, and I’ve ended up turning down invitations from family and skipping my usual yoga classes, hikes, and potlucks. I even had to postpone my dream trips to Oaxaca and Kyoto because I'm just too keyed up to go. Even my quiet hobbies like gardening, reading, and embroidery are ruined because I can't focus, leaving me feeling like I'm just constantly rechecking work instead of actually living my life.

Do you experience significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to persistent and excessive worry that is difficult to control, or are your symptoms more related to a specific traumatic event or stressor?

Yes, it has caused major issues in both my job and my personal life, but it isn't from a traumatic event; it started after taking on my demanding library promotion a year and a half ago. Since then, the uncontrollable worry has spiraled into other areas of my life, causing me to miss internal deadlines and turn down family invitations just to stay home and recheck my work.
Do you often find yourself worrying about multiple things at the same time, such as work, finances, health, or relationships, and does this worry feel like it's consuming most of your days?

Yes, it absolutely consumes my days, jumping from work worries like typos in grants or corrupted files to fearing I'll lose my job or haven't saved enough for my nieces' college. Even when I'm trying to relax in my garden, I get trapped in these endless "what ifs" about my staff burning out or workflows failing, and I just can't seem to shut them off.
Have you experienced any discrete episodes of intense fear or anxiety that reached a peak within minutes, such as panic attacks, in addition to your ongoing worries?

No, I haven't experienced those kinds of sudden, intense panic attacks. My anxiety feels much more like a constant, heavy background worry and physical tension that just persists throughout the entire day rather than hitting me in sharp peaks.
